attacks.question: Is this actually multi-agent, or one prompt in six hats?
attacks.risk: If every agent reads the same context and writes the same shape, the architecture is decoration.
attacks.fix: Each agent must write a distinct artefact to the blackboard, and later agents must depend on it.

attacks.question: Could this increase anxiety?
attacks.risk: A readiness score that can go down is a new thing to fail at.
attacks.fix: Readiness only counts completed items. It never decreases for inactivity, and open items are framed as optional.

attacks.question: Is the ELI5 bot too generic?
attacks.risk: A bot that gives the same answer to everyone is a search engine with better manners.
attacks.fix: Answers must reference the user’s own documents and end in the specific next action the Planner queued.

timeline.role: Rewrites copy and protects the tone
timeline.title: Set the tone for 5 user questions
timeline.detail: 3 of them switch humour off entirely.

Calm.when: The user is unsure, confused, or asking a first question.
Calm.style: Short sentences. No jokes. One next step.
Calm.example: No worries — this is a common thing to be unsure about. Let’s look at one part of it.

Helpful.when: Default mode for everyday preparation and discovery.
Helpful.example: 💡 Did you know? Naming a document is most of the work. The maths can wait.

Celebration.when: A preparation step the user chose has just been completed.
Celebration.style: Energetic, specific about what was achieved, never about money.
Celebration.example: 🎉 That is your first document saved. Your future self just avoided ten minutes of panic.

Sensitive.when: Distress, penalties, debt, disputes, missed deadlines, or legal worry.
Sensitive.style: No humour at all. Direct, calm, human. Route to a person.
Sensitive.example: I’m sorry — that sounds stressful. Let’s take the most urgent part first, and I’ll stay with it.
